correctness.rationale: The exact log pgf is a compound-Poisson generating polynomial in u_t=z_t-1, with c1=xi+mu alpha/S and c_j=mu(alpha)_j/(S)_j for distinct visits j>=2. Consequently c1,...,cT characterize the entire joint law; equations r=(alpha+2)/(S+2), s=(alpha+3)/(S+3) and s-r=beta/((S+2)(S+3)) imply strict beta-shape inverses and explicit positive feasibility conditions. Recovered second moment gives mu and mean gives xi. For T=3 the S perturbation preserves every coefficient and positivity near any xi>0, so produces equal full distributions; the two given rational models are checked by independent Poisson-mark intensities. With externally fixed xi=0 the first three coefficients invert uniquely, and two remain generically nonidentifying. Exact finite verification from included verify.py corroborates but is not substituted for the proof. Boundary xi=0 is included for four-visit inversion; alpha,beta,mu=0 excluded.

originality.rationale: Published model components and the multivariate-Poisson decomposition are acknowledged as prior art. The assessed joint claim is exact injectivity of the full anonymous joint count law at four visits, sharp generic failure at three with explicit equal full distributions, and admissibility inequalities for four cross-cumulants, under unknown independent Poisson false counts and persistent beta per-individual detection. Direct title, phrase, parameter, alias, reduction and stronger-coverage searches against published-finding corpus and source literature located no implication deriving this full conjunction. Residual risk is nonzero, especially an inaccessible older beta-mixture full text and generic compound-Poisson identification theory; failed search by itself is not treated as proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Repeated anonymous wildlife counts combine three distinct problems: unobserved abundance, persistent biological detection heterogeneity, and spurious counts. The theorem resolves a concrete experimental-design identifiability question with a sharp distinction between three and four visits even if arbitrarily many independent sites are observed. The full-law counterexample rules out any population-level estimator under only three visits; the exact feasible cumulant region additionally offers a mathematical diagnostic for a correctly specified beta-background model. The structural result is meaningful without finite-sample optimality claims and is not a trivial reparameterization of the constant-detection N-mixture because two independent beta moment ratios are required.
